## What's new since 1.0.0-alpha

### Items and weapons on the JXPilot server
- All 21 XPilot items work on the Java server: pick them up, drop them, and use the weapons and devices
  they give, checked against 12 recorded games of the original C server.
- Missiles (smart, heat seeking, torpedo), mines, lasers, nuclear and cluster weapons and the other
  weapon modifiers (implosion, velocity, mini, spread, power, laser stun/blind), with modifier and lock
  banks.
- Cloak and sensors, ECM, tractor and pressor beams, transporter, deflector, phasing, hyperjump,
  emergency thrust and shield, autopilot, armor, mirror, fuel tanks; cannons fire and defend with
  weapons too; player locks and viewing through a lock.

### Game modes on the JXPilot server
- Ball games: steal the enemy ball with your connector, tow it home and destroy their treasure;
  `captureTheFlag`, `treasureKillTeam` and the other treasure options.
- Targets: damage, destroy and repair them; `targetSync`, `targetKillTeam`, `targetDeadTime`.
- Races: checkpoints, laps, lap times, race scoring and ball races.
- Asteroids that drift, break up and score; temporary wormholes from hyperjumps; `gameDuration`, with
  the server shutting down 30 seconds after the game is over.
- Checked against 4 more recorded games of the C server.

### Commands, operators and alliances on the JXPilot server
- XPilot's `/` commands in the talk line: `/help`, `/team N`, `/ally ...`, `/get OPTION`, `/version`,
  `/queue`, `/lock`.
- Operators (`/password`, with `-password`, the config file or a `passwordFileName` file) can
  `/set` options while the game runs, `/kick`, `/pause`, `/reset` and `/lock` the game.
- Alliances (`allowAlliances`, `announceAlliances`) and custom ship shapes (`--shape`, `--shipShapeFile`,
  `allowShipShapes`).
- The client does not yet show the race score column or temporary wormholes.

### Maps built in
- The 19 standard XPilot maps are inside both jars and the apps: `--map tourmination` (or any of
  them) works with nothing else on disk, `--list-maps` lists them, and the server plays `default`
  when no map is given, as XPilot does. The maps zip is now optional.

### Sound
- Sound effects for XPilot's 82 sound events (22 public-domain clips), through OpenAL.
- `--sound` / `--no-sound`, `--volume 0..255` (or `maxVolume` in `~/.xpilotrc`), and the `-` key to
  mute. Most original XPilot servers are built without sound and send none.
- Each release now also carries the source of OpenAL Soft (`openal-soft-source-<commit>.tar.gz`), as
  its LGPL licence asks.

### Keys and controls
- Key bindings from `~/.xpilotrc` in the XPilot client's format (or `--keys FILE`); `--list-keys`
  prints them; `F1` shows a key help overlay in the game.
- New default keys: Alt/Option also connects to a ball, `0` also self-destructs (for Mac laptops).
- Turn speed now starts at 40. The power and turn speed keys work and show their meters.
- The HUD shows your weapon modifiers; refuel and repair beams are drawn.

### Server
- XPilot's `lib/defaults` is read at every start, as in XPilot (stronger gravity, softer walls, item
  settings); `--defaults FILE|none` changes that.
- `-help`, `-version`, `-dump` and the other information flags; `denyHosts`; `serverHost` as the bind
  fallback; `god:` messages to the operator's admin file; `logRobots`; wreckage; the map visibility and
  radar options.
- Robots that run out of lives leave and are replaced; robots react to how they were killed, as in
  XPilot.

### User guide
- "What you see on screen": a picture of every map feature, object and HUD element.
- Item icons and descriptions; every server option with its status on the Java server; a "Differences
  from XPilot" appendix.
